hypotheses.observation: The row transform uses three separate reduction phases over length-4096 rows, with no separated graph-site reuse.
hypotheses.mechanism: Phase boundaries may add kernel-launch and intermediate-memory traffic; row locality can be retained across phases without changing the required max-subtraction semantics.
hypotheses.transformation: Fuse the three phases into a row-oriented tiled implementation that uses the available row-sized scratch tile while preserving the existing reduction and numerical behavior.
preconditions: The input can be reread between phases or retained in tiles.
Reduction order and precision remain within the stated forward and backward error limits.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potentially fewer launches and less intermediate traffic, with benefit dependent on whether launches or arithmetic/reduction work dominates.
risks: Tile rereads may increase input bandwidth.
Fusion may reduce occupancy or increase synchronization cost.
Exact numerical behavior may change if reduction ordering changes.
unknowns: The relative cost of launches, memory traffic, exponentials, and reductions is unknown.
required_evidence: Measure per-phase kernel time, launch overhead, and global-memory traffic.
Validate forward max absolute error and backward relative error against the numerical contract.

hypotheses.observation: Full-row retention could avoid rereading values across the three phases, but only one row-sized scratch tile is available and full-row retention is not guaranteed.
hypotheses.mechanism: Materializing the complete row may reduce memory rereads, but its required storage and occupancy cost conflict with the stated scratch constraint.
hypotheses.transformation: Down-rank or defer full-row materialization unless memory-capacity and occupancy measurements show it is feasible.
preconditions: Sufficient storage exists for the entire row per active work item.
The added storage does not materially reduce occupancy.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Conditional reduction in reread traffic, but feasibility and net performance are currently unsupported.
risks: The required full-row buffer may be unavailable.
Extra storage can reduce occupancy or increase allocation pressure.
It may violate the intended scratch-memory constraint.
unknowns: Actual available persistent storage and occupancy impact are unknown.
The input reread cost is unknown.
required_evidence: Measure feasible per-row storage at target occupancy.
Measure memory traffic and runtime with and without full-row retention.

hypotheses.observation: The numerical contract requires strict max-subtraction semantics, while the facts do not establish whether an alternative online or reordered reduction is acceptable.
hypotheses.mechanism: A streaming or online normalization could reduce passes or storage, but it may change max-subtraction and reduction-order semantics and therefore numerical results.
hypotheses.transformation: Defer online softmax/log-sum-exp-style reformulation pending numerical equivalence testing; do not assume it is beneficial.
preconditions: The reformulation is proven to preserve the required max-subtraction semantics.
Forward and backward error remain within the stated bounds.
Its runtime and bandwidth are measured on the target workload.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potentially fewer storage requirements or passes if valid, but benefit and admissibility are currently unproven.
risks: It may violate strict numerical semantics.
Different reduction order may exceed error limits.
Additional compensation or synchronization may erase any speedup.
unknowns: Whether the contract permits mathematically equivalent but differently ordered evaluation is unknown.
Performance of the alternative formulation is unknown.
required_evidence: Compare outputs and gradients against the strict reference.
Measure pass count, runtime, and memory traffic on representative rows.
